correctness.rationale: The root equation |(P+tB)⊖sB|=πs² is a precisely cited 2006 theorem. Support halfplanes identify erosion as P+(t-s)B or P⊖(s-t)B, hence the threshold A=πt² and exact rational supra-threshold h. The small-erosion area A-Lu+Cu² follows from offset side shortening, and the implicit equation has derivative −(L+2πT)≠0. Independently expanded coefficients give the stated jump. Jensen gives C>π. The standalone checker reconstructs eroded polygons by clipping and checks 16 polygon cases, but the proof does not rely on numerics.

value.rationale: The derivative jump is not an arbitrary chosen polygon sample: it is valid for every genuine convex polygon and detects an intrinsic angle functional from the Cheeger response to physical Minkowski rounding. It identifies a universal sharp geometric phase transition and the exact order of loss of smoothness at the self-Cheeger boundary, refining the known differentiability theorem. This provides a usable shape-sensitivity benchmark for nonsmooth convex geometries.
